title: Kung Pao Chicken
summary: Velveted chicken thigh is stir-fried hard with dried chillies, Sichuan peppercorns and peanuts in a sweet-sour soy sauce.
equipment: wok (35 cm) or large frying pan (30 cm)

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1.5 cm dice
Chinese black vinegar, or rice vinegar
dried red chillies, snipped in half, seeds shaken out
spring onions, whites cut into 2 cm lengths, greens sliced

steps.title: Velvet the chicken
steps.text: Mix the chicken with the soy sauce, cornflour and water, and leave for 15-30 minutes. This light starch coating protects the meat during fierce heat, keeping it silky, and helps the finished sauce cling.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl and set aside.

steps.title: Toast the chillies and peppercorns
steps.text: Heat the wok over high heat until smoking, then add the oil and swirl. Take it off the heat if very hot, add the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns, and stir for 15-20 seconds until the chillies darken a shade and smell toasty - stop before they turn black, as burnt chillies turn bitter.

steps.title: Sear and stir-fry the chicken
steps.text: Return the wok to high heat, add the chicken and spread it out, leaving it for 1 minute to sear before stir-frying for 3-4 minutes until no pink remains and it reaches 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Add aromatics and sauce
steps.text: Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites and stir for 30-60 seconds. Stir the sauce again, pour it in, and toss for 30-60 seconds until glossy and thickened.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Take off the heat and toss through the peanuts and spring onion greens. Serve immediately with rice.

tips: Watch the chillies closely as they toast - a few seconds too long turns them bitter rather than fragrant.
Common mistake: adding the peanuts too early, which makes them soggy. Stir them in right at the end, off the heat, to keep them crunchy.
Velveting the chicken briefly in cornflour and soy keeps it tender through the high heat of stir-frying.
Have the sauce mixed and the aromatics prepped before you start cooking, since the stir-fry itself moves quickly.
Serve straight away; the glossy sauce and crunchy peanuts are best enjoyed fresh from the wok.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot wok or pan until piping hot (74°C (165°F)), as the peanuts will soften if reheated in a microwave. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour on a day above 32°C (90°F)).
